header: Cornerstone Coffee Co. — Website Content Checklist

blocks.text: Cornerstone Coffee Co. — Local Business Web Service

Use this checklist to gather everything we need before and during the build. The more complete your materials are upfront, the faster we can launch and the better the site will represent your business.
These items define your visual identity and must be provided before design work begins.
Client Action: Gather and send via the link or method your project contact shares.

items: Primary logo as a vector file (SVG preferred) or high-resolution PNG (at least 1000px wide)
Square/icon version of your logo for social media and favicon (PNG, 512×512 minimum)
Any variant you use (horizontal, stacked, with/without tagline)
If you don't have a logo yet, we can discuss a referral to a designer as a separate project

blocks.text: Why it matters: The logo appears on every page — header, footer, and social links. A vector file ensures it looks sharp on any screen size.

items: Your primary brand color (hex code, e.g. #3B2314) — this is the dominant color on the site
Your accent color (hex code) — used for buttons, highlights, and links
Any secondary colors you use consistently (optional)
If you don't have defined brand colors, we'll propose a palette based on your logo and industry

blocks.text: Why it matters: Your brand colors drive the entire site's look and feel. Once set, they're applied automatically across all pages and components.
Priority: Preferred before design begins; can be finalized during review.

items: Your primary display font (for headlines) — must be available on Google Fonts to keep the site fast and free
Your body font (for paragraphs and labels) — also from Google Fonts
If you don't have brand fonts, we'll recommend a pairing that suits your business type

blocks.text: Why it matters: Google Fonts are free, fast to load, and work on every device. Using fonts outside Google Fonts adds cost and complexity for no benefit on a small business site.
Priority: Optional — we can recommend a pairing if you don't have preferences.
These are the facts about your business that appear throughout the site. Accuracy here directly affects trust and search visibility.

items: Your exact business name as it should appear on the site and in search results
Any abbreviation or DBA you'd like noted (e.g. 'Cornerstone Coffee Co. — est. 2019')
A one-sentence summary of what you do and who it's for (e.g. 'Small-batch coffee, brewed for the neighborhood.')
If you don't have a tagline, we can write a draft for your review

blocks.text: Priority: Required — appears in the hero section of the homepage.

items: A 2–4 sentence description of your business — what you offer, where you're located, what makes you different
This appears in search result snippets (Google, Bing) and on the homepage — write it for a potential customer, not for yourself

blocks.text: Priority: Required — used for SEO meta description and homepage intro.

items: Phone number — include country code if outside the US/Canada (e.g. +1 503-555-0142)
Email address — the address where you want contact form submissions to arrive
Street address (if you have a physical location customers visit) — full address including city, state, ZIP
If you're a service-area business without a public storefront, tell us — we'll handle this differently for SEO

blocks.text: Priority: Required for contact page, map, and local SEO.

items: Opening and closing time for each day you're open (e.g. Monday: 7:00 AM – 6:00 PM)
Note any irregular hours, holiday hours, or days you're closed — we'll mark these on the site
If your hours change seasonally, let us know so we can plan updates

blocks.text: Priority: Required if you have a physical location customers visit during specific hours.
Links to your active social profiles appear in the header and footer. Only include profiles you actually use and update.

items: Instagram profile URL (if you use it)
Facebook page URL (if you use it)
TikTok, YouTube, LinkedIn, or any other platform you'd like linked (optional)
If you don't have social profiles yet, that's fine — we won't add empty links

blocks.text: Priority: Optional, but recommended — social proof and engagement help local SEO.
The services section is often the most-visited page after the homepage. Be specific — vague service descriptions lose customers.

items: Each service or product category you want listed (e.g. 'Espresso Drinks', 'Pour-Over Coffee', 'Cold Brew')
A 1–3 sentence description for each service — what it is, what makes it good, who it's for
Pricing for each service, if you're comfortable sharing it (starting prices work fine if exact prices vary)
If you offer packages or bundles, list them separately
If you prefer not to list prices, we can use 'Starting at $X' or 'Contact for pricing'

blocks.text: Why it matters: Customers often decide within seconds whether to call or visit based on whether they see what they need and what it costs. Clear service descriptions reduce wasted calls.
Priority: Required for the services page.
Photos are the single biggest factor in how professional your site looks. Stock photos are a fine placeholder, but real photos of your business convert far better.

items: 5–10 photos of your business, products, or team — the more the better
Preferred format: JPEG or PNG, 1200px on the longest side minimum, 2500px maximum
Orientation: a mix of landscape (for homepage hero, about section) and square/portrait (for gallery) works best
Accepted subjects: interior shots, exterior/storefront, product close-ups, team members, customers (with permission), detail shots of your work
If you have photos taken by a professional photographer, those are ideal — give us the highest-resolution versions you have
If you don't have photos yet, we'll use clearly-marked stock photo placeholders that you can replace later
Photos with heavy filters or editing that changes the actual appearance of your product or space
Photos you don't have rights to use (screenshotted from Google, other businesses' websites, or social media)
Blurry, dark, or heavily compressed images — a few good photos are better than many bad ones
Logos or branded items from other businesses visible in your photos (unless it's intentional, like a coffee bag on a counter)

blocks.text: Priority: 3–5 photos minimum for launch; 5–10 ideal. Stock placeholders accepted if real photos aren't ready.
Testimonials build trust and improve conversion. We can display them as manually-entered quotes or pull them from your Google Business Profile reviews — or both.

items: 3–6 short testimonials (1–3 sentences each) from real customers
For each: the quote text, the customer's first name (or full name if they've agreed), and their role or relationship to you (e.g. 'Regular since 2020', 'Morning regular', 'Laptop worker')
If you have photos of the customers who gave testimonials, those are a bonus but not required
Make sure you have permission from each person to use their quote on your website

blocks.text: Priority: 3 testimonials minimum for launch; 5–6 ideal.

items: If you'd like to show a live feed of your Google Business Profile reviews on the site, we'll need your Google Business Profile to be claimed and verified
We'll set up the widget — you don't need to do anything technical for this
Note: the Google reviews widget is an optional enhancement and may require a small monthly fee from the review platform; we'll confirm before enabling it

blocks.text: Priority: Optional — manual testimonials are a fine alternative.
Your site integrates with a few external services. You own each of these accounts — we'll set them up or connect them during the build, but they're yours to manage.

items: A Formspree account (free) — we'll guide you through creating one and setting up a contact form
Once created, you give us the form ID and we configure the site to submit to it
You'll receive an email to confirm the form before it goes live
Formspree's free tier handles 50 submissions/month — more than enough for a local business contact form

blocks.text: Priority: Required for the contact form to work. We'll walk you through setup.

items: A Calendly account (free) — we'll guide you through creating one and setting up your event type
Once created, you give us your Calendly booking page URL and we embed it on the site
Only needed if you offer appointments, consultations, or bookings

blocks.text: Priority: Optional — only if you want a booking widget on your site.

items: Your Google Business Profile claimed and verified — this is your business listing on Google Maps and in search results
If you haven't claimed it yet, we'll guide you through the process — it takes 10–30 minutes and requires a postcard, phone, or email verification from Google
A verified profile is one of the single biggest factors in showing up in local search results and Google Maps

blocks.text: Priority: Strongly recommended — essential for local visibility. We'll help you claim it if you haven't.
You may want to know how many people visit your site and what they do. We can set up analytics during the build or later.

items: Plausible Analytics (recommended for most small businesses): a simple, privacy-friendly analytics tool. Free trial, then $9/month per site. We'll set it up — you just give us the account or we create one for you.

Google Analytics 4 (GA4): free, more detailed, but more complex. If you want it, we'll set up the property and install the tracking code. Note: GA4 requires a Google account and takes longer to set up.
No analytics: perfectly fine — many small business sites don't need detailed traffic data. The site works exactly the same either way.

blocks.text: Priority: Optional — we recommend Plausible for simplicity, but it's your choice.
Your domain is your address on the web (e.g. cornerstonecoffee.co). It's one of the few things you truly own — keep it registered in your name.

items: Your domain name — either one you already own, or one you'd like to purchase
If you already own a domain: the registrar where it's registered (e.g. Cloudflare, Namecheap, GoDaddy) and your login access — we'll guide you through pointing it to your new site

If you need to buy a new domain: we recommend buying through Cloudflare (~$10–13/year, near wholesale) or Namecheap. Register it in YOUR name, not ours. We'll guide you through the purchase and DNS setup.
Important: never let an agency or developer register a domain on your behalf and keep it in their name. If they leave or go out of business, you lose your domain. Always register in your own name.

blocks.text: Priority: Required for launch — the site can be built and reviewed on a staging URL first, but the custom domain is needed to go live.
You can use your domain for professional email (e.g. hello@cornerstonecoffee.co). This is optional and separate from the website build.

items: Your preference: Zoho Mail (free tier available, good for a single user or small team) or Google Workspace ($6/user/month, familiar if you already use Gmail)
The email addresses you want created (e.g. hello@, info@, yourname@)
We'll guide you through setting up the email service and configuring your domain's DNS records so email delivers correctly
Email setup is a separate service from the website build and may incur its own cost depending on the provider and complexity

blocks.text: Priority: Optional — many businesses use a personal Gmail or other existing email during early stages and add professional email later.
Before launch, you'll review the site on a private staging URL. This is your chance to catch anything that needs to change.

items: We send you a link to a private staging version of your site — it looks and works exactly like the live site, but only people with the link can see it
You review on your own time and note anything you'd like changed
We include 2 rounds of revisions in the build fee — a 'round' is one batch of changes, not one change at a time
Revisions cover: text corrections, photo swaps, color tweaks, layout adjustments, and broken links. They do not cover adding new sections, new pages, or features not in the original scope.
After the 2 revision rounds, any additional changes are billed at our standard hourly rate unless you're on a Care Plan retainer

blocks.text: Priority: You'll receive the staging link during the build. Plan for 1–2 hours to review thoroughly.
Send everything in one place — scattered emails and messages get lost.

items: A shared Google Drive folder — we'll create one and send you the link. Drop all files there. This is the preferred method for photos and logo files.
A single email with everything attached — fine for text content and small files
A shared spreadsheet (Google Sheets) — useful for services, testimonials, and hours if you have a lot of data
Whatever works for you — we'll adapt to your workflow, but one place for everything keeps things from getting lost

blocks.text: File naming: please name files clearly (e.g. 'logo-primary.svg', 'coffee-shop-interior-1.jpg', 'testimonial-mara.jpg'). Avoid 'IMG_4829.jpg' without context.
A typical build takes 5–7 days from the time we have all content plus 1–2 business days for each revision round.

rows: We send the content checklist; you gather and submit materials; we confirm scope and pricing
We customize the site with your content, brand colors, and photos; you get a staging link
You review the staging site and send feedback; we make up to 2 rounds of revisions
We connect your domain, verify SSL, and make the site live; you get final handoff documents

blocks.text: Delays usually come from missing content — the checklist exists to prevent that. The faster you get us complete materials, the faster we launch.
If anything on this checklist is unclear, or you're not sure what we need, just ask. We'd rather answer a question early than have you spend time gathering things we don't need.
